coverage.method: For each result, match only the exact repository file paths assigned to that slice. Parse inclusive numeric intervals and comma-separated numeric interval lists following the path colon; ignore descriptive parenthetical or semicolon suffixes. Intersect each interval with its assigned primary interval, union overlaps, and calculate the complement. Ignore nonassigned context files. No application source files were opened during consolidation.
limitations: Complete is the reviewers' declaration. The independently calculated interval union verifies that declaration against the slice assignment, not actual primary reading, review quality, or defect completeness.
Tool-read execution and displayed source content were not independently audited. No missing primary reading is inferred from this limitation.

Some reviewer evidence cites context outside assigned slices or current external proxy configuration. Such context is not counted as primary coverage and is not independently bound to code_sha by this consolidation.

consolidation_policy.activity: Mechanical consolidation only; no new defect search, application changes, execution probes, or counterchecks.
consolidation_policy.candidate_id: W02-<slice>-<lens>-<one-based finding index within the final result>
consolidation_policy.canonical_id: Use the first selected member by stable ID, except that the four existing A01/B02/B03 canonical IDs remain unchanged.
consolidation_policy.source_locator: For each member_id, remove its last numeric component to identify the review in model_proofs. Read the model proof's journal_result_line and result.findings[index-1] to recover the exact original structured finding. The source journal and each transcript have SHA256 proofs. No raw transcripts are copied into the repository.
consolidation_policy.field_fidelity: Group prose condenses existing reviewer results. Exact original claim, class, file, line, scenario, evidence, expected behavior and countermeasures remain addressable by source_locator for every member. Distinct scenarios and C-policy uncertainties are retained below.
consolidation_policy.verification: Only the four named canonical claims inherit existing briefing status. Other original candidates, including duplicate reports, have received no new independent countercheck. Inherited confirmation does not certify supplemental member assertions or imply that a fix is finished.
separate_related_causes: Refresh reinsertion, stale cache refill, central import reinsertion, ignored durable logout cookie and failed DELETE remain separate.
Historical chat/tag analytics and AI-history/monetization login-reuse scenarios remain separate because their storage and ownership predicates differ.
Rate-hit retention and expired-session/OAuth-state retention remain separate; shared-table janitor overlap is not established.
CSRF, rate-limiter and session-fixture setup failures remain separate helpers and retain their original B/C proposals.
SQL waits in chat cleanup, audit insertion, rate limiting and session refresh remain separate policies and callers.

groups.claim: A stale first master_dash_session cookie makes successful admin mutations lose their authenticated Discord actor in the audit log.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Successful admin configuration POST with expired first and valid second master_dash_session cookie belonging to Discord user 42 stores actor=admin instead of discord:42. Separate Cookie headers can produce the same mismatch.

groups.evidence: admin_audit.rs:54-88 selects only the first cookie; :110-130 computes and persists that actor. auth/level.rs:408-474 and its test :872-917 accept the later valid cookie. handlers/admin_audit_log.rs:674-699 exposes the stored actor.
groups.expected_behavior: The valid session that authenticates the mutation determines the known Discord audit actor.
groups.countermeasures: Auth and CSRF already handle later valid cookies; the routing contract and audit writer permissions do not correct the independently resolved actor. No privilege escalation or live incident is claimed.

verification_status.scope: Canonical claim only; inherited, not re-evaluated. Fix completion not assessed.

groups.claim: Without a PostgreSQL statement timeout, one locked expired chat can indefinitely disable follow-up reservations.

failure_scenarios.scenario: An uncommitted maintenance transaction locks an expired chat row. Background cleanup and a follow-up DELETE occupy both analysis-writer connections when SQL/lock timeouts are disabled; every reserve first runs global cleanup, disabling unrelated conversations until the lock is released.

groups.evidence: ai_store.rs:83-126 runs cleanup without an execution deadline; :185-187 awaits it before reservations. Existing test :445-486 releases an expired-row blocker manually. lib.rs:2041-2054 limits the writer pool to two connections. ops/systemd/twitch-runtime-roles.sql:361-402 supplies no SQL execution timeout.
groups.expected_behavior: A finite cleanup execution budget would isolate unrelated conversations. Retention is explicit, but the execution budget and timeout policy are unspecified, so the proposal remains C.
groups.countermeasures: Acquisition deadlines do not release already acquired connections. close_on_drop handles cancellation but no production deadline initiates it. CleanupTask aborts only when its final owner disappears. Provider deadlines and the separate lock pool do not bound cleanup SQL. Deployed database/DSN timeout settings were not inspected and could mitigate this. Consider an explicit cleanup SQL deadline only after deciding policy.

groups.claim: Without a PostgreSQL statement timeout, a blocked audit INSERT withholds an already successful admin response indefinitely.

failure_scenarios.scenario: An ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on dashboard_admin_audit_events blocks the audit INSERT after a covered admin mutation has succeeded. Without SQL timeouts, middleware retains the completed response and a connection until lock release.

groups.evidence: admin_audit.rs:91-94 calls auditing best-effort; :118-136 awaits insertion before returning the completed response. lib.rs:2245-2248 installs the middleware. tb-dashboard/src/main.rs:400 and tb-db/src/pool.rs:20-58 use a normal pool, not the read-only statement-timeout mode.
groups.expected_behavior: Best-effort persistence should not indefinitely prevent delivery of an already completed response. The required latency budget and permission to drop timed-out audit events are unspecified, retaining class C.
groups.countermeasures: Logged INSERT errors preserve responses only once SQL returns. Acquisition timing does not bound SQL execution. Uninspected deployed role/database/DSN timeouts could bound the wait. Consider a finite audit budget while preserving handler success. Similar to chat cleanup's unbounded wait but a separate operation and policy.

groups.claim: The first OBS dock can silently lose events while the database listener is starting.

failure_scenarios.scenario: The first dock completes websocket replay before asynchronous PostgreSQL LISTEN becomes effective. Event E commits and notifies in that interval; first-start MAX(id) then includes E without replaying it. A healthy socket receives neither E nor a gap notice.

groups.evidence: lib.rs:1985-1992,2218 wires the bus. obs/ws.rs:484-497,757-764 starts LISTEN without awaiting readiness and independently replays. obs/bus.rs:393-405,440-458 spawns LISTEN and initializes a first-start watermark without catch-up. tb-bot/src/obs_dock.rs:205-236 writes events and notifications.
groups.expected_behavior: obs/ws.rs:15-19 and :42-53 require a buffered or explicitly reported replay/live gap.
groups.countermeasures: The startup flag prevents duplicate listeners, not readiness races. Broadcast subscription protects only forwarded events; reconnect/Lagged recovery is not triggered. The existing websocket helper omits the real DB listener. BRIEFING-B02 conditions the scenario on obs_docks.enabled=true; deployment settings and live incidents were not established.

verification_status.scope: Canonical first-start claim only; inherited, not re-evaluated. Fix completion not assessed.

groups.claim: The cancellation route uses a literal ü and does not match browser requests to /twitch/abbo/k%C3%BCndigen.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A browser GET or authenticated, CSRF-valid POST sends the advertised cancellation URL with percent-encoded ü; the native router registers only the Unicode literal and returns 404 instead of cancel_handler.

groups.evidence: lib.rs:1662-1665,2231 registers the literal. handlers/billing_page.rs:938 advertises it. Locked Axum path_router.rs:388,490-505 matches URI paths without percent decoding.
groups.expected_behavior: The advertised URL reaches the cancellation handler; POST validates CSRF and cancels while GET redirects without cancellation, per billing_page.rs:315-351.
groups.countermeasures: No encoded alias or percent-decoding middleware was found in the inspected assembly. Auth/CSRF follows route matching. Handler-only tests bypass routing. An optional legacy fallback may mask, but does not repair, native route matching. Static reviewer evidence only.

groups.claim: The native website router redirects /streamer to an unregistered /streamer/ route.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A native /streamer request redirects to /streamer/, which returns 404 when legacy fallback is disabled because the wildcard cannot match an empty path. Native /website/ has the same empty-wildcard gap. No public website outage is established.

groups.expected_behavior: Native trailing-slash roots should serve their index according to lib.rs:1995-2002 and handlers/website.rs:194-209. Whether native root delivery is required on real ingress is unresolved, retaining C.
groups.countermeasures: Public proxy routing may mask this. ops/tests/partner_profiles_caddy.test.mjs:44-52,90-92 intentionally leaves /streamer and /streamer/ on landing/static delivery rather than forwarding to this backend. Confirm a real native-ingress requirement before treating this as a public failure.

groups.claim: An oversized OAuth expires_in permanently terminates the unsupervised proactive refresh task.

failure_scenarios.scenario: With configured Kick/YouTube clients and a due enabled connection, an HTTP 200 token response containing expires_in=9223372036854775807 is accepted. Chrono expiration conversion panics; the discarded spawned-task handle leaves all scheduled refreshes stopped until restart.

groups.evidence: lib.rs:2276-2297 discards the JoinHandle. handlers/plattform_oauth.rs:103-126,137-162 accepts unrestricted i64 expiry. platform_token.rs:538-543 calls Duration::seconds. Locked chrono time_delta.rs:208-216 panics beyond i64::MAX/1000; rust/Cargo.toml:125-130 permits unwinding. Callback twin: plattform_connect.rs:348-349,419,470.
groups.expected_behavior: Malformed provider expiry becomes a refresh error while the Result-based scheduler continues subsequent ticks.
groups.countermeasures: max(0) only handles negative values; a 35-second store timeout does not catch panic. Provider configuration, DB constraints and rollback do not validate numeric expiry. No task supervision/restart was found in this assembly. Static, unconfirmed candidate.

groups.claim: The proactive refresh loop reports credentials renewed when their provider client is absent.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A saved Kick or YouTube connection is due, but after restart that provider's credentials/client are absent while Twitch still enables the scheduler. Every five minutes it reports a renewal despite no provider request or DB update and unchanged expiry.

groups.evidence: platform_token.rs:82-108 accepts optional clients; plattform_oauth.rs:173-175,398-400 returns absent clients. platform_store.rs:311-324 selects due rows. platform_token.rs:555-557,575-577 returns Ok without work; :361-368 counts it as renewed; lib.rs:2288-2290 logs success.
groups.expected_behavior: The renewal count and message represent actual renewal, not skipped attempts.
groups.countermeasures: Request-time platform_token.rs:476-488 refuses expired credentials with absent clients, preventing delivery but not false scheduler success. Both providers share the counting path.

groups.claim: Transient OAuth refresh failures are silently discarded by the scheduled refresh loop.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Configured Kick/Google providers repeatedly return 503 while database reads work. All due refreshes fail, but scheduler gets Ok(0), logs no warning and retains unchanged credentials; later credential requests can return 502.

groups.evidence: plattform_oauth.rs:137-151 returns an unlogged Other error; platform_token.rs:546-550 drops details. platform_store.rs:433-435 maps it to Fehlgeschlagen; platform_token.rs:597-603,361-368 discards it through is_ok. lib.rs:2291 ignores Ok(0), bypassing its warning arm.
groups.expected_behavior: A sanitized operational diagnostic or failure aggregation would preserve observability while other connections continue. Exact best-effort aggregation/logging policy is unspecified, so C.
groups.countermeasures: Retries every 300 seconds and request-time refusal of expired credentials prevent silent credential delivery, not diagnostic loss. SQL errors are logged separately. Preserve no raw provider body without considering secret disclosure. A logging/aggregation contract requires a decision.

groups.claim: The shared CSRF layer rejects valid one-time partner-login sessions.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A fresh partner-link login sets only twitch_dash_session_partner; same-browser GETs work but same-origin silent-settings POST returns invalid_csrf, even with the durable session's correct token.
Only the valid durable cookie is present; engagement/mode POST is rejected before either empty CSRF candidate loop can validate it.
engagement/mode POST with output_mode=off fails after fresh durable login; reopening the login link recognizes the existing durable session and redirects without recovering writes.
A durable-only login cannot save streamer/onboarding with paused=true despite working authenticated GETs.
A fingerprint-matched active durable partner cannot save silent settings; auth-status also exposes no CSRF token for this branch.
silent-settings POST with silent_ban=true and silent_raid=false returns invalid_csrf even when the durable CSRF value is supplied.
A fresh external durable-login browser cannot POST valid title/settings JSON because its partner_token cookie is ignored.

groups.evidence: All members identify the same missing durable-cookie/session-type branch in auth/csrf.rs:55-83,122-167. handlers/partner_login.rs:325-365 creates only that cookie; auth/level.rs:371-394 authenticates it as Partner; auth/session.rs:695-739,1878-1953 creates/validates it. lib.rs:496-510,632-635,749-750,1003-1015 attaches the shared CSRF layer. Engagement, onboarding, silent-settings and title handlers expressly permit own-channel Partner writes. Source member anchors also include csrf.rs:78,122 and level.rs:385.
groups.expected_behavior: A valid device-bound durable Partner login permits the same allowed own-channel, same-origin writes under CSRF protection as other Partner logins; it is not documented as read-only.
groups.countermeasures: HMAC, atomic one-time login consumption, fingerprint checks, expiry, active-partner gates and origin checks validate login but cannot make its cookie visible to CSRF. Normal/admin cookies or loopback access can mask the failure, but fresh public-browser durable login has neither. A CSRF header cannot rescue an absent candidate. No conversion layer was found in the reviewer-traced assembly. This is denied authorized behavior, not an auth bypass.

groups.claim: The partner-link route ignores valid configured internal admin credentials.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A direct localhost POST to partner/link carries the correctly configured X-Internal-Token, no browser cookies and a valid body, but returns admin_required because ExpectedToken is absent from that router.

groups.evidence: lib.rs:1475-1499,2207-2210 receives only pool/limiter and adds no ExpectedToken or promotion layer. main.rs:476-587 adds session/OAuth configuration but not ExpectedToken. auth/level.rs:329-344 delegates to tb-http-core middleware/auth.rs:96-107, which requires that extension. partner_login.rs:102-107 denies None.
groups.expected_behavior: The documented Admin/Localhost link-issuance route supports correctly configured internal-token authentication, per lib.rs:1467-1468, partner_login.rs:6-10,94 and tb-http-core middleware/auth.rs:39-49.
groups.countermeasures: Cookie admins still work and origin checks remain. Session extensions and layers on other merged routers do not supply this route's expected token. Direct loopback bypasses proxy allowlists. Denied legitimate operation only; no bypass claim.

groups.claim: Bounded query integers outside i64 return 400 instead of clamping.

failure_scenarios.scenario: An authorized weekly-stats request uses days=9223372036854775808 or -9223372036854775809; it receives 'must be an integer' 400 instead of clamping to 3650 or 7.
An authorized category-activity-series request supplies the same over/underflow integers; monthly stats shares the helper and rejection instead of numeric saturation.

groups.evidence: query_int.rs:47-58 parses i64 before clamp. :6-13,35-39 documents integer-and-clamp semantics and :81-86 tests only representable out-of-range values. performance.rs:44-50,78-80,206-218 and category_activity.rs:38-40 retain raw query strings and propagate the error. lib.rs:789-791,855-857 wires these routes.
groups.expected_behavior: Syntactically valid decimal integers saturate at documented bounds even when the raw number cannot fit i64; only nonintegers receive the integer error.
groups.countermeasures: Auth rejects unauthorized callers but accepts the scenario's authorized request. Option<String> extraction performs no earlier normalization. Existing overflow tests use values fitting i64. No legacy Python reading or execution was required for the reviewers' documented Rust-contract claim.

groups.claim: Dashboard fallback responses bypass the documented 16 MiB body limit.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Enabled fallback fully buffers and successfully returns an upstream 17 MiB body; runaway responses can exhaust memory instead of generating a controlled proxy error.
An unmatched GET receives a 32 MiB chunked upstream response within 120 seconds. Large or concurrent responses exceed process memory despite the response-budget contract.

Configured legacy fallback returns 32 MiB from a nonnative endpoint within its timeout; concurrent oversized responses can exhaust dashboard memory, without an established attacker-controlled generator.

groups.evidence: proxy.rs:60-66 documents response OOM protection. MAX_BODY_BYTES is used only for incoming requests at :147; :202-214 collects unrestricted resp.bytes. main.rs:497-511 installs the conditional fallback. All three reports cite the targeted legacy_proxy.rs:121 twin but do not establish that separate component's full coverage or response-limit contract.
groups.expected_behavior: Enforce the documented 16 MiB response ceiling during incremental reading, including absent Content-Length, before retaining the full oversized response.
groups.countermeasures: A 120-second total timeout, disabled redirect following, disabled-by-default fallback, native-route precedence and incoming-body limits do not bound upstream bytes when fallback is enabled. Later response compression cannot undo collection. No deployed reachability, attacker-controlled large response or class-A exploit was established; raw reviewer use of 'confirmed conditional bug' is not an independent countercheck here.

groups.claim: A stalled incoming body can hold a dashboard fallback request indefinitely because the upstream timeout starts only after body collection.

failure_scenarios.scenario: With fallback enabled, a direct client declares a 16 MiB POST body, sends 8 MiB and remains open. Incoming collection stays pending beyond 120 seconds, retaining buffers/connections; repeated stalled uploads never contact upstream.

groups.evidence: proxy.rs:147 awaits to_bytes before constructing/sending the request at :159,192; the :97-98 reqwest timeout therefore excludes ingress collection. main.rs:497-608 supplies no incoming deadline/concurrency limit. proxy.rs:28-29 explicitly supports direct loopback requests.
groups.expected_behavior: A finite ingress-body deadline would release stalled requests. Only the upstream deadline is contracted; upload-rate and ingress-deadline policy remain unspecified, so C.
groups.countermeasures: The 16 MiB input bound limits one body's size, not pending duration or concurrent uploads. Client disconnect releases the request, but this scenario stays connected. An uninspected gateway might impose additional limits, without protecting explicitly supported direct loopback ingress.

groups.claim: Concurrent DB test runs sharing a database can drop each other's fixed fixture schemas.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Two copies of coaching_ohne_plus_403_mit_plus_200 share TB_TEST_DATABASE_URL. The second drops t_gate_coaching after the first seeds it, causing missing/recreated-table failures. Concurrent public comparison tests have the same fixed-name collision.

groups.evidence: plan_stufen_gates.rs:100-131 recreates schema and :196-202 uses a fixed name. public_streamer_comparison.rs:30-50,105 repeats it. Neither helper uses run-unique naming or a cross-process lock.
groups.expected_behavior: Independent runs should not destroy each other's fresh fixtures; however, same-database concurrent invocations are not explicitly guaranteed, so this is C test isolation, not a production defect.
groups.countermeasures: Distinct names isolate different tests within one invocation. search_path and single-connection fixtures do not prevent cross-process schema deletion; router-local cache synchronization is unrelated. Separate databases or external serialization prevent the scenario, but invocation-level protections were not established.

groups.claim: The empty Twitch ID in the shared partner fixture makes plan acceptance tests fail identity guards before their intended feature gates.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Configured DB and unbookable Creator Pro: auto_posting_offen_solange_pro_nicht_buchbar receives 403 on its first batch upload instead of expected success; clip_kontingent_zaehlt_ohne_zu_sperren similarly fails before upload/quota gates.

The same empty-ID partner fixture fails the positive upload path and paid-coaching/scope-dependent success cases before intended plan assertions; social access and clip-owner fixtures also remain login-only.

groups.evidence: plan_stufen_gates.rs:138-143 creates empty twitch_user_id. social_media.rs:505-524,1416-1418,1512-1515 invokes the guard; tb-social-media partner_access.rs:19-22 rejects empty IDs before SQL. streamer_scope.rs:150-153 and coaching.rs:51-62 also require stable IDs. Test access schema/grants :71-73,281-288 and clips :292-296 omit ID linkage.
groups.expected_behavior: Positive acceptance fixtures represent valid authorized stable-ID partners while independently controlling plan state; they must reach posting, quota and scope-dependent plan assertions without weakening production guards.
groups.countermeasures: Production guards correctly fail closed; login-only grants cannot override immediate empty-ID rejection, and direct handler calls cannot obtain identity from middleware. Merely fixing the helper ID does not fix login-only access/clip schemas. The quota-only test that never calls a social handler is not implicated by the correctness report. Missing DB configuration silently skips relevant tests. Static evidence only; no tests were run.

groups.claim: A concurrent sliding refresh can recreate a partner session after logout.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Cold-cache same-origin tokenless CSRF fallback reads a partner session due for refresh. Logout deletes it and clears caches; the pending INSERT then recreates it and caches auth, allowing later replay beyond cache TTL.
A two-hour-old six-hour partner session is read; logout completes before a refresh whose drift exceeds 1800 seconds. The same retained cookie works after row reinsertion and cache refill.
An active partner session due for persistent refresh is read before completed logout, then upserted under the same bearer key with a fresh six-hour expiry.
Logout DELETE/cache removal completes between payload read and refresh INSERT; a copied cookie authenticates after both logout and five-second cache expiry.
A retained partner cookie starts a due refresh; concurrent owner logout deletes the row before the earlier request recreates it, extending validity another six hours.

Normal Twitch partner R1 reads with empty cache, R2 completes logout, then R1 permanently recreates the same key. This is subsequent independent access, not just completion of an already-authorized request.

groups.evidence: session.rs:1773-1807,1993-2014 reads without a read/delete/refresh transaction. :2072-2115 refreshes old payloads through INSERT ON CONFLICT. :1854-1858 can refill caches. invalidate_session :1511-1527 and DELETE :2043-2050 are separate. auth_login.rs:724-753 reaches logout; auth/level.rs:353-367 and csrf.rs:146-156 reach loaders. session.rs:3506-3544 asserts sequential invalidation. Other admin/durable callers share the helper but their complete exploitability is not independently established by every member.
groups.expected_behavior: Successful logout keeps the credential server-side invalid for subsequent requests; pending refresh must neither reinsert a deleted row nor recache it merely because renewal failed. Existing valid-session TTL/cache/identity contracts are preserved by the inherited A01 scope.
groups.countermeasures: Cache locks cover individual operations, not the interleaving. Primary key and hash constraints permit a deleted identifier to be inserted again; encryption authenticates the stale payload, not continued validity. Active-partner checks do not record revocation; cookie clearing affects one browser, not retained copies. The race requires due refresh. No actual cookie theft, browser-cookie recovery, live replay or production exploitation is claimed. Stale cache fill without refresh is a separate unreviewed group.

verification_status.scope: Canonical partner-refresh resurrection claim only. Duplicate reports have no additional counterchecks; other session-type exploitability and standalone stale-cache race are not promoted. Fix completion not assessed.

groups.claim: Both IDOR E2E fixtures leave their required operator Twitch ID unconfigured.

failure_scenarios.scenario: With a test DB, the Partner test gets adminEligible=false instead of true; the Discord test's public master session becomes None rather than Partner. Both fixtures fail before later IDOR/CSRF regression checks.

Partner fixture :224-235 supplies ID 42. Production main.rs:517-518 explicitly sets the ID.
groups.expected_behavior: Positive operator-eligible fixtures configure their matching immutable ID; the unconfigured application must remain fail-closed.
groups.countermeasures: Missing test-DB configuration skips tests and masks failure. ENV/schema fields cannot set this private state field. This is a static existing-fixture candidate, not a test failure newly caused by a fix or an executed test result.

groups.claim: The same-origin comparison rejects matching IPv6 hosts.

failure_scenarios.scenario: Host=[2001:db8::1]:8767 and Origin=http://[2001:db8::1]:8767 normalize differently: request_host removes brackets and url_host retains them. A protected write is classified CrossOrigin and receives 403 before session/CSRF checks.

groups.evidence: csrf.rs:206-208 strips IPv6 brackets; :195-196 keeps Url::host_str and :243-252 compares strings. Locked url-2.5.8 src/lib.rs:1126-1130 documents bracketed IPv6; Cargo.lock:4722-4723 binds that version.
groups.expected_behavior: Matching IPv6 hosts should compare like matching IPv4/DNS hosts. IPv6 parsing suggests intent, but a supported production IPv6-literal dashboard ingress is unproven, so C.
groups.countermeasures: Direct loopback can bypass origin checks, not the example's nonlocal address or forwarded requests. DNS-host access is unaffected. A proxy host allowlist might exclude IPv6 literals entirely; deployed IPv6 reachability was not investigated. No runtime test was run.

groups.claim: Configured database setup failures silently pass all four database-backed CSRF regression tests.

failure_scenarios.scenario: An explicitly configured test DB fails connection, CREATE SCHEMA or table setup. maybe_test_state returns None and all four callers return successfully without persisted-session/CSRF assertions.

groups.evidence: csrf.rs:469-521 converts setup errors with .ok()?; :570-572,600-602,630-632,643-645 returns on None. Neighbor IDOR helper :54-113 skips only absent configuration and fails configured setup; auth/level.rs:770-823 similarly fails schema/pool/table errors.
groups.expected_behavior: Optional absent configuration may skip; configured setup failures must fail, not certify unexecuted assertions.
groups.countermeasures: Non-DB tests still run but cannot prove persisted sessions, tokenless same-origin writes or stale-admin-cookie recovery. Other tests may fail during a full-suite outage but do not protect a filtered run. No setup failure or skip diagnostic is emitted by these callers.

groups.claim: CSRF middleware discards session-store errors and reports them as invalid_csrf.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A valid same-origin Partner write reaches a cold/expired session cache during a temporary PostgreSQL outage. Loader errors become false/None; middleware emits 403 invalid_csrf without the DB diagnostic.

groups.evidence: csrf.rs:130-156 uses unwrap_or(false) and .ok().flatten(); :166 emits the generic response. session.rs:1531-1550 documents error propagation; :1780-1782,2013-2014 propagates failed queries. lib.rs:1005-1015 places CSRF before the public partner gate.
groups.expected_behavior: Continue failing closed but preserve an operational diagnostic and, if permitted, distinguish infrastructure errors from invalid credentials. Status/disclosure policy is unspecified, so C.
groups.countermeasures: No auth bypass is alleged. Warm caches or another valid cookie can rescue a request; admin gates may reject earlier. These do not retain the underlying error on the traced cold-cache public write path. An API disclosure/status decision is required.

groups.claim: Duplicate session cookies multiply database timeout waits in the CSRF middleware.

failure_scenarios.scenario: A public engagement/mode POST with permitted Host, X-CSRF-Token=x and 100 identical invalid admin cookies reaches an exhausted DB pool. Each duplicate separately tries token validation and admin loading; five-second acquisitions can retain it for roughly 1000 seconds unless an outer layer cancels.

groups.evidence: csrf.rs:55-82 collects duplicates; :130-160 retries them after errors. session.rs:1537-1551,1570-1585,1993-2014 performs two acquisitions per nonempty-token invalid admin candidate. lib.rs:632-635,1003-1015 exposes the guard before partner auth. tb-db pool.rs:20-58 only bounds each acquisition.
groups.expected_behavior: Fail-closed 403 is documented, but no aggregate auth deadline or duplicate-cookie limit is specified. Excessive failure-path duration remains C, not a proven production DoS or an automatic B fix.
groups.countermeasures: A selected-session extension limits candidates, but this public router runs CSRF before auth. Empty tokens omit one lookup; the example uses a nonempty token. Pool limits/deadlines do not bound aggregate time. Effective production proxy cancellation was not verified. Choosing an aggregate deadline requires policy review.

groups.claim: A concurrent central admin session import can restore an admin session after successful logout.

failure_scenarios.scenario: After positive-cache expiry, A validates a central admin session; B then successfully revokes it centrally and deletes the local mirror/caches. A sees no local row and imports its previously validated snapshot. Later retained-cookie requests work, including forward-auth; explicit broker rejection falls back to the recreated row after cache expiry.
